transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, I came in because I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. It could be something at work, like a wrong number in a data release, or just an unlocked back door at home, or a bill paid from the wrong account. 

And the thing is, even when I know I checked it—and I know I did—my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some sort of disaster. It's just... it's become really hard to function with it.
When these thoughts hit, do you find yourself repeatedly checking things to feel sure?

Yes, I do. Just to try and calm myself down, I end up reopening the same spreadsheets I've already closed. I'll reread emails line by line. Or with the other things, I'm checking the locks, or pulling up payment confirmations over and over. 

I usually have to do it in a specific set order, too, and I keep going until it finally feels safe. It takes up so much time. Some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, just doing these checks, with absolutely nothing actually finished.
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors feel excessive or unreasonable to you?

Yes, they definitely do. I mean, I work with numbers and data all day, so I know logically that checking a cell in a spreadsheet for the sixth time isn't going to change the math. It's completely excessive. I know that. 

But... knowing it doesn't really stop the feeling. Even though I know it's unreasonable, I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it anyway.
When you do the checking, is it mainly to relieve the anxiety from those unwanted thoughts?

Yes, exactly. I mean, like I mentioned before, I end up reopening the same spreadsheets or rereading emails line by line just to try and calm myself down. It's the same with checking the locks or looking at payment confirmations over and over. I do it in that set order, and I just keep doing it until I finally get that feeling that it's safe. It's the only way to get the anxiety to stop, even though it means I'm stuck at my desk for hours getting nothing done.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I definitely get frustrated with myself—and just exhausted, really—because of how much time I lose to all this checking. But I don't feel down or depressed most of the day. It's more just... just the anxiety and feeling stuck in that loop, rather than actually being depressed.
Did these symptoms start soon after a specific stressful event or major life change?

No, not really. I mean, I've tried to trace it back to something specific, but there wasn't any big event or sudden change that set it off. It just sort of... crept up on me over time. It started small and just got worse and worse until it became this whole routine. So, no, nothing specific triggered it.
Outside of these checking-related thoughts, do you spend a lot of time worrying about many other everyday things?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things like anyone else, but it's not something that consumes my time. The real issue is just... the constant checking and the thoughts about making a mistake with the numbers or leaving something unlocked. That's what takes up all my time and energy. I don't really sit around worrying about other everyday stuff.
